tldr: Names and measures the Degeneration-of-Thought (DoT) failure of single-agent self-reflection — confidence locks in wrong answers — and fixes it with Multi-Agent Debate (MAD): two 'tit-for-tat' debaters plus a judge with adaptive break, lifting GPT-3.5-Turbo past GPT-4 on commonsense MT.
method: The paper names DoT: once an LLM is confident in an answer, self-reflection stops generating novel thoughts even when the initial stance is wrong, quantified as adjacent-iteration opposition over 5 forced rounds (Fig. 1): self-reflection's disagreement stays low while debate keeps it high. MAD runs three agents: an affirmative debater, a negative debater prompted to 'disagree with the affirmative side's points', and a judge. Debaters speak in fixed order, each conditioned on the full debate history H. The judge has two modes: discriminative (is a correct solution on the table? True ends the debate early, the adaptive break) and extractive (pull the final answer from H at the iteration limit, set to 3). All roles share one backbone LLM (vicuna-7b/13b-v1.5-16k, GPT-3.5-Turbo-0301, GPT-4-0314), zero-shot at temperature 0; tasks are Common MT (Chinese⇒English commonsense ambiguity) and the authors' 200-question Counter-Intuitive AR set.
results: Common MT human direct assessment (1-5), GPT-3.5-Turbo baseline → +MAD vs GPT-4: lexical 3.14 → 3.78 (GPT-4 3.41), contextless 3.43 → 3.67 (3.63), contextual 3.57 → 3.67 (3.65) — MAD on Turbo beats GPT-4 on all three, and on COMET/BLEURT it matches or edges GPT-4 (contextual COMET 85.3 vs 85.0); Self-Reflect reaches only 3.43 lexical
Counter-Intuitive AR accuracy: 26.0% (Turbo) → 37.0% with MAD, vs Self-Reflect 27.5%, CoT 28.0%, Self-Consistency 29.5%; GPT-4 stays ahead at 51.0%
DoT mitigation vs Self-Reflect: human-labeled ambiguity-error (bias) 29.0 → 24.8 and output diversity (100 - Self-BLEU) 19.3 → 49.7
Math/symbolic transfer (Turbo, Appendix C): MAD vs CoT — GSM8K 73.8 vs 70.2, AddSub 92.1 vs 87.3, BBH Date 65.2 vs 56.4, Penguin 63.7 vs 58.9; cost 2.46x CoT's generated tokens (Self-Reflect 1.83x)

Ablations (Sec 4): debater quality dominates judge quality (Turbo debaters: 3.47 HUMAN with a vicuna-13b judge vs 3.69 with a Turbo judge); the judge favors its own backbone (GPT-4 judging GPT-4-vs-Turbo picks the GPT-4 side 120/200 vs 77); more debaters hurt (2 → 3 → 4: COMET 84.4 → 83.1 → 82.9); modest level-2 'tit for tat' beats full consensus (HUMAN 3.00 → 3.81) and forced total disagreement (0.988 disagreement, 3.72)
advantages: First to name and operationally measure DoT (adjacent-iteration disagreement), turning 'self-reflection plateaus' into a diagnosable failure with a causal account — bias, rigidity, missing external feedback — each mapped to a mechanism of the fix
Divergence by construction rather than hope: the negative debater is instructed to oppose, so the loop cannot quietly agree with itself the way Self-Reflect does (diversity 49.7 vs 19.3)
The judge's adaptive break ends most debates after one round and outperforms forcing any fixed iteration count (Fig. 5), keeping overhead at 2.46x CoT tokens

Reports the negative results later debate work leans on — adding debaters hurts, forced disagreement backfires, LLM judges favor their own backbone — and states the mitigations (modest tit-for-tat, one LLM for all roles) in the limitations
limitations: Time/compute cost of multi-round interaction: 2.46x CoT's generated tokens on Counter-Intuitive AR, vs 1.83x for Self-Reflect (Sec. Limitations, Appendix E)
Long-context degradation: with more debaters, 'LLM-based debaters tend to forget the views of other debaters' and judge extraction degrades — 2 debaters beat 3 and 4 (Table 7)
LLM judges are not impartial across backbones (self-preference, Table 6); the authors recommend identical LLMs for judge and debaters
Counter-Intuitive AR is the authors' own 200-question set (elicitation questionnaires + web puzzles), and MAD does not close the gap to GPT-4 there (37.0 vs 51.0)
fits: Stage 6: the diagnostic companion to Du et al.'s debate paper (2305.14325) — debate instrumented against self-reflection with a named failure mode (DoT) and a judge-plus-adaptive-break control loop. Its 'other agents beat self-feedback' argument underwrites the multi-agent arc toward debate-generated training data; pair with Reflexion as the single-agent foil.
